messages:
ashley: Heads-up — started seeing ~30% of APAC GPU nodes go Unhealthy around 03:12 UTC. Alert: node-exporter scrape failures + kubelet failing to pull keystore secrets.
ashley: errors in node logs show TLS handshake timeouts to keystore endpoint and `connection refused` to prometheus scrape port 9100.
matt: 👀 did we roll any firewall/stateful rules recently in ap-southeast?
ja: yes, pushed a tighter egress stateful policy last night (PR #478). It was intended to block a couple of legacy flows to reduce audit surface.
ashley: that matches timing. I can see `conntrack: DROP` entries correlated with the node restart timestamps.
kevin: can you paste the exact `iptables`/conntrack lines?
ashley: ```
conntrack: DROP src=10.2.5.12 dst=10.37.8.2 sport=54032 dport=9100 proto=6
conntrack: DROP src=10.2.5.12 dst=10.48.9.10 sport=49152 dport=443 proto=6
```
ops-runner: deploy-bot shows the egress policy change deployed at 02:58 UTC to `apac-tight-egress` via `terraform apply`.
deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: apply complete. 3 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed`
sre-bot: Alert correlation: prometheus scrapes failed for 18 nodes between 03:09–03:16 UTC. KMS decrypt errors for node bootstrap observed for 12 nodes.
matt: KMS decrypt errors — are nodes unable to reach keystore because of the same egress policy? Which destination?
ja: the keystore is a private endpoint at 10.48.9.10:443 — PR tightened egress allowed list to only specific subnet ranges, forgot to include the keystore CIDR for new subnet allocation. My bad.
ashley: consequence: nodes couldn't retrieve instance role secrets -> kubelet started failing health checks -> node went NotReady -> controller scaled up replacement nodes -> we hit GPU allocation pressure and some pods evicted.
kevin: immediate mitigation: revert the egress rule or add the keystore CIDR + allow 9100 scrape from prometheus.
jia: I can flip a partial rollback in <5m. Which option do we want: full rollback or targeted allowlist update?
matt: targeted allowlist is safer. Add these two entries:
```hcl
egress_allow = ["10.48.9.0/24:443", "10.37.8.0/24:9100"]
```
ops-runner: rolling the allowlist now via `terraform apply -target=module.egress.apac` (ETA ~90s).
ashley: confirming prometheus scrapes are returning for an initial node (10.2.5.12) — `curl http://10.37.8.2:9100/metrics` -> 200 OK. KMS decrypts succeeding for new node bootstraps.
kevin: good. Remaining items: audit why PR missed that CIDR, update preflight checks, and add a canary for egress changes that verifies keystore + node-exporter connectivity.
ja: proposing a preflight step: run `egress-checker` that attempts TCP connects to a small set of internal endpoints (keystore, node-exporter endpoints) before applying. I'll open PR.
matt: also, add an alert rule that watches KMS decrypt failure rate and flags before node status flips.
ashley: tracking impact: ~27 pods were rescheduled, 3 GPU workloads timed out and retried. Estimated cost hit: ~1.4 GPU-hours extra and 0.8k egress audit logs for the remediation window.
kevin: timeline notes for postmortem: 02:58 terraform apply, 03:09 first node-exporter drops, 03:12 KMS decrypt errors surface, 03:18 ops-runner allowlist update applied, 03:21 scrapes restored and bootstraps succeed.
ops-runner: I've tagged PR #480 with the rollback diff and linked the egress-checker issue: infra#1124.
ja: I'll add a unit to the runbook: "egress change checklist" and include `curl` checks and `kubectl get nodes` sanity gate.
sre-bot: Reminder: please create incident doc in `incidents/` with severity S2 and include logs + aws flow logs.
ashley: will create incident doc and grab conntrack dumps. Assigning owners: remediation done (jia), postmortem (ashley), follow-up preflight (jia), alert rule (matt).
kevin: thanks everyone — reopen if anything flaps. :thumbsup:
